paragraphs: Generative compressed sensing reconstructs a high-dimensional signal from relatively few measurements by assuming that the signal belongs to the output range of a generative model. This paper studies nonlinear measurements, including observations that are quantized, discontinuous, or governed by an unknown transformation. Its main concern is whether one measurement setup can support recovery across the entire modeled signal family.

Earlier guarantees often concern a single fixed signal. The authors develop a framework for uniform guarantees: the same realization of the sensing system works simultaneously for all signals in the specified generative range. Using generalized Lasso, recovery to error at most epsilon requires roughly k divided by epsilon squared measurements, apart from logarithmic factors, where k is the latent dimension.

This measurement requirement nearly matches existing guarantees for individual signals, suggesting that uniformity adds little cost within the analyzed setting. The technical tools include Lipschitz approximations for discontinuous observations and a concentration inequality for suitably structured product processes. Experiments provide additional support for the theory.
neurips-2023-a-unified-framework-for-uni.tldr: A unified framework gives nearly the same measurement requirements for recovering an entire generative signal family as for recovering a single fixed signal.

paragraphs: This paper develops an optimization method for smooth, convex objectives without constraints. It uses only gradients, while maintaining matrices that approximate second-order information about the objective. The central question is whether such quasi-Newton information can deliver a provable improvement over Nesterov’s accelerated gradient method in this setting.

The algorithm combines a variant of the Monteiro–Svaiter acceleration framework with an online learning approach to updating its Hessian approximations. Those updates are analyzed as decisions in a matrix-valued online optimization problem. The authors connect the resulting dynamic regret to the convergence of the original optimization method, giving a way to translate approximation quality into a convergence guarantee.

The proven rate is the smaller of 1/k² and √(d log k)/k²·⁵, up to constant factors. Here d is dimension and k is iteration count. It matches the accelerated gradient rate in the stated earlier regime and improves on it once iterations reach the order of d log d. Thus, the gain is dimension-dependent and emerges with sufficiently many iterations.
neurips-2023-accelerated-quasi-newton-pr.tldr: A gradient-only quasi-Newton method provably improves on accelerated gradient convergence after a dimension-dependent number of iterations.

paragraphs: Producing convincing images does not directly reveal how well a model understands relationships between objects and language. This paper makes that question more measurable by adapting Stable Diffusion to image–text matching. The resulting method, DiffusionITM, lets a generative model participate in tasks designed to test whether images and descriptions agree.

The authors also introduce GDBench, which combines seven complex vision-and-language tasks with bias evaluation and detailed analysis. This creates a shared evaluation route for generative and discriminative models. Stable Diffusion paired with DiffusionITM is competitive on many evaluated tasks and exceeds CLIP on compositional tasks including CLEVR and Winoground.

Fine-tuning on MS-COCO further improves compositional performance while preserving image generation capabilities. The bias analysis finds that Stable Diffusion 2.1 is generally, though not uniformly, less stereotypically biased than version 1.5. Together, these findings show that diffusion models contain capabilities that can be assessed through matching tasks, giving a more specific picture of their strengths than image quality alone.
neurips-2023-are-diffusion-models-vision.tldr: DiffusionITM turns Stable Diffusion into an image–text matcher, revealing competitive performance and particular strengths on evaluated compositional tasks.

paragraphs: Adapting a pretrained model with only a small number of additional parameters addresses the cost of transferring knowledge to new tasks. This paper also targets the cost of running the adapted model. Conditional Adapter, or CoDA, combines parameter-efficient transfer with conditional computation so that inference speed becomes part of the adaptation design.

CoDA starts from an existing dense pretrained model, introduces sparse activation, and adds relatively few new parameters. A lightweight training phase prepares this modified model for the target task. The sparse activation provides a way to vary computation, creating a balance between speed and accuracy while retaining the parameter efficiency associated with adapter methods.

Across the reported language, vision, and speech experiments, CoDA runs inference two to eight times faster than the compared state-of-the-art adapter approaches. Accuracy losses range from moderate to none, with the same parameter efficiency. The results therefore support a practical benefit across several modalities, while making clear that faster inference can still involve an accuracy tradeoff.
neurips-2023-conditional-adapters-parame.tldr: CoDA combines sparse activation with lightweight adaptation to achieve reported inference speedups of two to eight times, with moderate to no accuracy loss.

paragraphs: Training with incorrect labels requires deciding which labels to trust and which to replace. The paper argues that evaluating samples independently, largely through a model’s own predictions, overlooks useful relationships in the data. Those omissions can produce poor corrections and cause the model to keep learning from mistaken labels.

Curriculum and Structure-aware Optimal Transport, or CSOT, treats label allocation as a coordinated problem. Its formulation considers relationships within and between distributions, seeking labels that separate groups globally while remaining coherent locally. During training, the allocator progressively assigns reliable labels to a fraction of samples with the highest confidence, rather than correcting every sample at once.

The resulting optimization problem has a nonconvex objective and curriculum constraints, so standard optimal transport solvers do not apply directly. The authors develop an efficient solution using scaling iterations inside a generalized conditional gradient framework. Their experiments report stronger noisy-label learning performance than the compared state-of-the-art methods, supporting the value of combining structural information with gradual label assignment.
neurips-2023-csot-curriculum-and-structu.tldr: CSOT uses data relationships and progressive label assignment to improve learning from corrupted labels in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: This paper studies the fundamental prediction error achievable when regression must satisfy demographic parity under a linear model. Its focus is minimax error: the best worst-case performance available within the specified problem setting. That perspective asks how difficult the constrained learning problem is, rather than assessing only the behavior of one particular fitted predictor.

The proposed model includes a broader range of discriminatory bias sources than the earlier model identified in the abstract. Within this expanded setting, the authors establish that the minimax error scales as dM/n, up to constant factors. Here n is the number of samples, d is the feature dimension, and M is the number of demographic groups defined by sensitive attributes.

The rate describes how sample availability, dimensionality, and group count enter the problem’s statistical difficulty together. The analysis also shows that greater bias in the model increases minimax error. These conclusions concern demographic-parity-constrained regression under the studied linear model; they characterize its attainable error rather than asserting a universal relationship for every fairness criterion or model family.
neurips-2023-demographic-parity-constrai.tldr: Under the studied linear model, demographic-parity-constrained regression has minimax error scaling as dM/n, with greater model bias increasing that error.

paragraphs: Subgame solving improves a strategy by concentrating computation on a relevant part of a larger game. In imperfect-information games, however, the player’s uncertainty can leave that part extremely large. The paper addresses a remaining obstacle in approaches that already restrict the knowledge considered: information sets can still contain too many possibilities for convenient refinement.

The proposed generative subgame solving framework, GS2, uses a generation function to select a subset of the earliest-reached nodes. Restricting those starting possibilities reduces the size of the subgame to be solved. The authors support the framework with theoretical analysis and introduce a generation function based on diversity to improve safety.

Experiments cover medium-sized games and the much larger game GuanDan. The resulting strategies significantly improve on the blueprint, the strategy being refined. The contribution is therefore a way to make local strategy improvement more manageable in large games while considering the quality of the selected subset. The stated results support improvement over the blueprint without claiming that every possible selection is safe or optimal.
neurips-2023-efficient-subgame-refinemen.tldr: GS2 reduces subgame size by generating a subset of starting nodes and improves on blueprint strategies in the evaluated games.

paragraphs: Worldwide image localization must handle enormous geographic variety. Matching against a gallery would require extensive image coverage, while classifying images into fixed geographic cells can misplace locations far from cell centers. GeoCLIP instead learns to align images directly with representations of GPS coordinates, framing localization as image-to-location retrieval.

Its location encoder treats geographic position continuously. Random Fourier features provide positional encoding, and a hierarchy combines information at multiple resolutions. This produces a high-dimensional location representation that can be aligned with image features. The approach gives geographic coordinates a learned representation without making predefined cell classes the central prediction target.

Experiments and ablations on benchmark datasets support the method’s effectiveness. The authors also report competitive performance using only 20% of the training data, demonstrating usefulness in their limited-data setting. A qualitative demonstration extends localization to text queries through the image encoder’s CLIP backbone. That demonstration suggests an additional use of the shared representation, while the main evaluated contribution remains worldwide image geolocation.
neurips-2023-geoclip-clip-inspired-align.tldr: GeoCLIP aligns images with continuous, multiresolution GPS representations for worldwide localization, including competitive results with reduced training data.

paragraphs: Reconstruction-based anomaly detectors learn what normal images look like and use reconstruction behavior to identify unusual inputs. A problem arises when the model reconstructs abnormalities as effectively as normal content. This paper tackles that shortcut in a single model spanning multiple classes, avoiding the expense and limited generalizability of separate class-specific solutions.

The proposed Transformer represents typical normal patterns with discrete prototypes obtained through vector quantization. These prototypes guide reconstruction so that abnormal content is mapped toward normal content. This makes the representation of normality an explicit part of the reconstruction process, addressing the tendency of flexible continuous representations to reproduce both kinds of input well.

A hierarchical design addresses codebook collapse and strengthens weakly represented normal patterns. The method also uses prototype-oriented optimal transport to regulate prototypes and evaluate anomaly scores across the hierarchy. On MVTec-AD and VisA, the authors report performance above the compared state-of-the-art alternatives and good interpretability. The findings support discrete, structured normal prototypes as a useful basis for unified anomaly detection.
neurips-2023-hierarchical-vector-quantiz.tldr: A hierarchical Transformer uses discrete normal prototypes to counter reconstruction shortcuts and improve multi-class anomaly detection.

paragraphs: Adaptive optimizers are often explained as adjusting to the overall geometry of a loss function, resembling methods that use second-order information. This paper argues that this account is insufficient for neural networks. It instead examines the local regions encountered along an optimizer’s path, asking whether different algorithms steer training into differently conditioned parts of the loss landscape.

The authors introduce a trajectory statistic analogous to the condition number of the loss Hessian at successive iterates. In language-model experiments where adaptive methods converge faster, Adam tends to visit regions with smaller values of this statistic. Momentum SGD tends to visit regions with comparatively larger values, where optimization might be expected to proceed less easily.

A theoretical result demonstrates the phenomenon in a simplified two-layer linear network. Together, the experiments and analysis support examining how an optimizer shapes its trajectory, alongside how it responds to geometry. The paper presents this as evidence for a revised explanation of adaptive optimization’s success, with the formal demonstration limited to the simplified network setting.
neurips-2023-how-does-adaptive-optimizat.tldr: Experiments and a simplified theoretical result suggest that adaptive optimizers favor training paths through more favorably conditioned local regions.

paragraphs: Prompt Diffusion explores whether an image-generation model can infer a visual task from an example. The input includes a task-specific pair of images, a new query image, and text guidance. The example pair communicates a relationship, such as transforming depth into an image or an image into a scribble, which the model then applies to the query.

The authors design a vision-language prompt that expresses multiple tasks in this common format and train a diffusion model to consume it. Training jointly covers six tasks. This shared prompt structure gives the model a consistent way to use visual demonstrations and language, allowing task information to be supplied through the current input.

The resulting model produces high-quality in-context outputs on the trained tasks and generalizes effectively to new vision tasks in the reported demonstrations. It also supports text-guided image editing. These findings show that demonstration-based task specification can work within a diffusion framework, while distinguishing the model’s joint training stage from its subsequent ability to respond to new example prompts.
neurips-2023-in-context-learning-unlocke.tldr: Prompt Diffusion learns to apply visual tasks from example image pairs and text, including reported generalization to unseen tasks.

paragraphs: MCUFormer addresses running vision Transformers on microcontrollers with extremely small memory budgets. The paper treats model architecture and inference implementation as a joint design problem. A network must fit the available memory, and the operations executing that network must use their temporary storage carefully enough for the forward pass to succeed.

The architecture component extends one-shot neural architecture search to optimize task performance subject to a device’s memory budget. Its search space includes low-rank decomposition dimensions and patch resolution, giving the search additional ways to reduce memory needs. The implementation component builds a Transformer operator library with explicit attention to buffer scheduling.

Operator integration, patch embedding decomposition, and token overwriting help reuse the available inference memory. Combining these choices, MCUFormer achieves a reported 73.62% ImageNet top-1 accuracy with 320 KB of memory on an STM32F746 microcontroller. This result demonstrates a concrete deployment under severe memory constraints and highlights why architecture selection and execution-level memory management need to be designed together.
neurips-2023-mcuformer-deploying-vision-.tldr: MCUFormer jointly optimizes Transformer architecture and memory use, reporting 73.62% ImageNet top-1 accuracy with 320 KB on a microcontroller.

paragraphs: Multiplication accounts for much of the computational work in neural-network training and inference. This paper investigates how far it can be replaced while still successfully training modern models. Its starting point is a cheap, piecewise affine approximation implemented by adding the integer interpretations of floating-point bit representations.

The authors use this approximation inside modified matrix multiplications and train Transformers on vision and language tasks. They report little to no performance impact in those experiments without changing training hyperparameters. This matters because it shows that replacing a central arithmetic operation can preserve useful learning behavior without requiring a separately retuned training configuration.

The work then extends beyond matrix multiplication. Replacing network nonlinearities makes the networks jointly piecewise affine in their inputs and weights, meaning their behavior is affine within individual regions. Finally, the authors remove multiplications throughout the forward pass, backward pass, and optimizer update. They demonstrate successful fully multiplication-free training, extending the feasibility result to the entire training process.
neurips-2023-multiplication-free-transfo.tldr: Piecewise affine arithmetic enables successful multiplication-free neural-network training, with little to no performance impact reported for modified Transformer matrix multiplications.

paragraphs: Sequential latent variable models describe observations through hidden states evolving over time. Flexible versions can be difficult to fit because the posterior calculations needed for learning are analytically intractable. NAS-X addresses this inference-and-learning problem with an approximate method designed for sequential structure, including models with either discrete or continuous hidden variables.

The method extends reweighted wake-sleep using smoothing sequential Monte Carlo to estimate posterior expectations. These expectations feed into the gradients used for learning. The combination produces estimates with low bias and low variance, targeting both systematic estimation error and the fluctuation that can make learning unreliable. The paper also develops theoretical advantages over earlier approaches.

Experiments examine those advantages across several tasks, including mechanistic models of neuronal dynamics. NAS-X substantially improves on the compared variational-inference and reweighted-wake-sleep methods in inference and model learning, with lower parameter error and tighter likelihood bounds. These findings indicate that improving sequential posterior estimation can translate into better recovery of model parameters and stronger likelihood-based assessments.
neurips-2023-nas-x-neural-adaptive-smoot.tldr: NAS-X combines reweighted wake-sleep with smoothing sequential Monte Carlo to improve inference and learning in sequential latent variable models.

paragraphs: Visual localization estimates a camera’s pose within a scene. Training strong localization systems can require many images with known poses and costly dense 3D labels. NeRF-IBVS reduces those supervision demands by using a small collection of posed images and scene information supplied by a neural radiance field, or NeRF.

The method first trains a coordinate regression network using coarse pseudo-3D labels from NeRF. A perspective-n-point procedure then converts the network’s output into an initial pose estimate. Finally, image-based visual servoing refines that pose using the NeRF scene prior. The pipeline therefore combines a coarse learned estimate with a subsequent pose-optimization stage.

On 7-Scenes and 12-Scenes, the authors report better performance than state-of-the-art methods under the same setting while using only 5% to 25% of the training data. The framework also supplies a prior for visual-servo-based navigation without custom markers or a depth sensor. Simulation experiments verify this navigation extension, while the dataset experiments establish the reported localization results.
neurips-2023-nerf-ibvs-visual-servo-base.tldr: NeRF-IBVS combines NeRF-derived supervision with visual servoing to localize cameras using fewer posed images and supports navigation in simulation.

paragraphs: Object-centric learning aims to organize visual information into representations associated with objects. This paper asks whether the expressive image-generation capabilities of diffusion models can improve that process, especially for complex scenes. It introduces Latent Slot Diffusion, or LSD, which conditions a latent diffusion image generator on learned object slots.

The diffusion model replaces the conventional decoder that reconstructs images from those slots. This makes the generator part of the object-centric learning system while also enabling compositional conditional generation without supervised annotations such as text. The shared design connects learning object-based representations with generating images from those representations.

Across the evaluated object-centric tasks, LSD significantly outperforms compared state-of-the-art Transformer decoders, particularly on more complex scenes, and produces stronger unsupervised compositional generations. The experiments also bring FFHQ into this evaluation setting. A separate preliminary investigation incorporates pretrained diffusion models and demonstrates effectiveness for real-world image segmentation and generation. Those initial results support further integration, while the principal evidence concerns the proposed slot-conditioned diffusion architecture.
neurips-2023-object-centric-slot-diffusi.tldr: Latent Slot Diffusion uses object slots to condition diffusion generation, improving evaluated object-centric learning and unsupervised compositional generation.

paragraphs: Text-to-3D methods can extract guidance from pretrained text-to-image diffusion models through score distillation sampling, or SDS. The paper identifies excessive saturation, excessive smoothing, and limited diversity as problems with this approach. It proposes variational score distillation, VSD, which models the 3D parameters as a random variable instead of a fixed quantity.

VSD uses a particle-based variational framework, with SDS appearing as a special case. The authors show poor SDS samples at both small and large classifier-free guidance weights, while VSD works well across different weights. At the common weight of 7.5, VSD improves both diversity and sample quality, addressing two aspects of generation together.

The complete ProlificDreamer system also changes the distillation schedule and density initialization, design choices separate from the distillation algorithm. It generates NeRF scenes rendered at 512 by 512 resolution with rich structure and effects such as smoke and drops. Meshes initialized from those NeRFs and refined using VSD are reported to have detailed, photorealistic appearance.
neurips-2023-prolificdreamer-high-fideli.tldr: ProlificDreamer uses variational score distillation and additional design improvements to produce higher-quality, more diverse text-guided 3D content.

paragraphs: Federated learning combines updates from participating clients, making malicious updates a threat to the shared model. Existing defenses can struggle to separate genuine but unusual client gradients from deliberately harmful ones. RECESS addresses both detecting malicious clients and combining client gradients in a way that reduces damage from model poisoning.

The method actively queries each client using a carefully constructed aggregation gradient and analyzes the response. This gives the defense an additional interaction on which to base detection. It then aggregates gradients through trust scores that account for relationships in client behavior across multiple iterations, rather than evaluating each iteration in isolation.

The authors report that this history-aware scoring improves tolerance to detection faults. Evaluation spans four datasets, typical model architectures, and settings including white-box and black-box attacks as well as cross-silo and cross-device federated learning. Against five classic and two state-of-the-art defenses, RECESS better reduces attack-induced accuracy loss in the reported experiments. The evidence supports stronger tested defenses without implying immunity to every poisoning attack.
neurips-2023-recess-vaccine-for-federate.tldr: RECESS proactively probes federated clients and tracks trust across iterations to reduce poisoning-related accuracy loss in evaluated settings.

paragraphs: Language-model agents can act in environments such as games, compilers, and APIs, but learning efficiently from failed attempts remains difficult. Reflexion gives agents a way to use trial-and-error feedback through language. The agent writes reflections on task feedback and stores them in an episodic memory buffer that informs decisions on later trials.

The framework changes the information available to the agent without updating the language model’s weights. Feedback can be a numerical score or free-form language, and it can come from an external source or an internally simulated one. This flexibility lets the same general process accommodate different kinds of task feedback.

Experiments report significant improvements over a baseline agent on sequential decision-making, coding, and language reasoning. On HumanEval, Reflexion achieves 91% pass@1 accuracy, compared with the cited previous GPT-4 result of 80%. Additional ablations examine feedback signals, incorporation methods, and agent types. These findings show that retaining and using written reflections can improve later attempts in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-reflexion-language-agents-w.tldr: Reflexion improves language-agent performance by storing written reflections on feedback and using them in subsequent attempts without changing model weights.

paragraphs: Time-series forecasting often separates changing trends and seasonality from a remaining stationary random component. Each stage has established methods, but analyzing them together is harder because estimation errors and correlated noise interact. SAMoSSA provides theoretical support for a two-stage procedure that combines multivariate singular spectrum analysis with autoregressive modeling.

The first stage estimates deterministic, nonstationary components using multivariate singular spectrum analysis, even when correlated autoregressive noise is present. The second stage learns that noise structure from the residual series. The authors establish a finite-sample forecasting consistency bound, addressing predictions beyond the observed data rather than only whether fitted parameters resemble the underlying model.

The analysis handles the matrix spectra of stable autoregressive processes and autoregressive identification under bounded perturbations. These results connect the two learning stages despite imperfect separation. The resulting procedure is data-driven and requires little parameter tuning. Representative experiments report improvements of 5% to 37% across benchmark datasets, supporting the practical value of modeling the autoregressive structure left after trend estimation.
neurips-2023-samossa-multivariate-singul.tldr: SAMoSSA gives forecasting guarantees for jointly handling nonstationary trends and correlated autoregressive residuals through a two-stage procedure.

paragraphs: In a changing environment, the world continues to evolve while a reinforcement-learning agent collects data and trains. This paper emphasizes that those changes occur in elapsed time, not according to episode number. Even with the same number of episodes, different interaction schedules can expose an agent to different trajectories and alter policy performance.

The Proactively Synchronizing Tempo framework, ProST, chooses interaction times by minimizing an upper bound on dynamic regret. Its schedule balances time spent training the policy against the speed of environmental change. The authors derive a suboptimal interaction sequence as a function of the environment’s degree of nonstationarity, rather than claiming to find the globally best schedule.

The analysis also establishes sublinear dynamic regret. In experiments across high-dimensional nonstationary environments, ProST achieves higher online return than existing methods at the derived schedules. The contribution makes timing an explicit part of learning: allocating additional training time can have different consequences depending on how much the environment changes before the agent interacts again.
neurips-2023-tempo-adaptation-in-non-sta.tldr: ProST adapts interaction timing to environmental change, balancing policy-training time with responsiveness and achieving higher reported online returns.

paragraphs: This paper studies generalization for stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics, asking how its performance on training data relates to performance beyond that data. Under smoothness and dissipativity assumptions, the authors derive bounds that do not worsen with the number of iterations. The bounds shrink toward zero as sample size grows, including when the step size stays fixed.

The analysis follows the time evolution of Kullback–Leibler divergence. This quantity connects dataset stability to an upper bound on the information that learned parameters retain about the input dataset. Tracking it provides the route to controlling generalization without accumulating an increasingly unfavorable dependence on training duration.

The authors also establish an information-theoretic bound for using the same loss in training and testing by showing that an SGLD loss is sub-exponential. This result remains time-independent and removes a problematic step-size dependence from existing work. Combining the generalization analysis with available nonconvex optimization bounds yields an improved excess-risk bound, linking statistical behavior to optimization progress under the stated assumptions.
neurips-2023-time-independent-informatio.tldr: Under smoothness and dissipativity, new SGLD generalization bounds shrink with sample size without deteriorating as training iterations increase.

paragraphs: Segmenting vessels or road networks involves identifying thin structures whose connections matter. Weak image signals and complicated branching make these tasks difficult, so experts often need to check automated results. This paper estimates uncertainty for pieces of connections and branches, aiming to highlight error-prone structures for human review.

The approach uses discrete Morse theory to extract the structures before assessing their uncertainty. One component jointly predicts uncertainty while considering neighboring structures, capturing how confidence in one piece relates to its surroundings. A second component, probabilistic discrete Morse theory, samples alternative representations through a perturb-and-walk procedure to model uncertainty within an individual structure.

These two components address complementary questions: how uncertain a structure is in context, and how uncertain its own representation is. Across several two-dimensional and three-dimensional datasets, the method produces better structure-level uncertainty maps than existing approaches. The result supports presenting uncertainty in units aligned with the connections annotators need to inspect, rather than relying solely on separate confidence values for individual pixels.
neurips-2023-topology-aware-uncertainty-.tldr: Topology-aware uncertainty estimates identify uncertain branches and connections to support expert review of vessel and road segmentations.

paragraphs: Real-world training sets can contain incorrect labels, duplicates, and biases that slow learning or interfere with convergence. Choosing samples solely because they appear easy or difficult may not handle all these issues together. This paper builds on the idea of choosing data according to its expected effect on generalization loss.

Earlier implementations of that principle relied on less principled approximations and additional holdout data. The proposed method addresses these obstacles through a lightweight Bayesian treatment combined with readily available zero-shot predictors built from large pretrained models. The resulting selection algorithm is described as efficient and straightforward to implement, making this generalization-oriented principle more practical.

The evaluation considers online batch selection on challenging benchmarks with substantial noise and imbalance. The method achieves better training efficiency than competitive baselines in these experiments. On WebVision, it reaches similar predictive performance with significantly fewer training iterations than leading data-selection methods. This finding supports more effective use of training updates, with the stated efficiency result specifically demonstrated through reduced iteration requirements.
neurips-2023-towards-accelerated-model-t.tldr: Bayesian data selection uses pretrained zero-shot predictors to choose useful training batches and reaches comparable WebVision performance in fewer iterations.

paragraphs: Semantic correspondence means finding locations in different images that represent the same meaningful object part or region. This paper uses semantic knowledge already present in a text-to-image diffusion model to perform that matching. It shows that this knowledge can be used without training the model for a correspondence task.

For a region in the first image, the method optimizes prompt embeddings to maximize attention on that region. Those embeddings capture semantic information associated with the selected location. Transferring them to another image then provides a way to locate corresponding content. The procedure therefore involves prompt optimization even though it does not require model training.

On PF-Willow, the reported results are on par with the strongly supervised state of the art. Across PF-Willow, CUB-200, and SPair-71k, the method significantly outperforms existing weakly supervised or unsupervised approaches, including a 20.9% relative improvement on SPair-71k. These results support using diffusion-model attention and optimized prompts as a bridge between image generation knowledge and semantic matching.
neurips-2023-unsupervised-semantic-corre.tldr: Optimized prompt embeddings extract semantic correspondences from Stable Diffusion without model training, outperforming compared weakly supervised and unsupervised methods.
